criteria.criterion: A test (run with cargo test) shows that with a PR whose head differs from the job's commit and is green while the job's commit is red, land does not report the old commit's failure and judges the head's checks; and when the head equals the landing commit, land merges.
criteria.evidence: land_pr_judges_the_current_head_not_the_old_commit passes: the checks log holds only fix1 (the green head), the error says 'checks of that head are green' and not 'are red', there are no reruns and no merge, and the stored head is fix1. land_pr_merges_when_the_head_is_the_landing_commit passes: merge_requested is true, one merge, and the link is Landed.

criteria.criterion: A test (cargo test) shows the merge request is guarded with the PR's current head sha, and that no push or update replaces a newer head with the job's older commit.
criteria.evidence: land_pr_guards_the_merge_with_the_current_head_and_pushes_nothing_over_a_newer_one passes. merge_heads is [cand1], read from remote_head (gh.rs:1312-1339). With the newer head fix1 there is no merge, the only push is the first publish of cand1, the remote still holds fix1, and the stored head is fix1. Remote::replace was removed from the trait.

criteria.criterion: A test (cargo test) shows land refuses when the PR head is anything other than the job's landing commit, including when the extra commit is a declared intervention, and the message names each extra commit and why it is refused (squash with later commit invalid until D111 records-history build).
criteria.evidence: land_pr_refuses_any_other_head_naming_each_extra_commit_and_why and land_pr_refuses_a_real_branch_with_a_declared_intervention_after_the_landing (real git with a bare remote) pass. The errors contain each extra commit's short sha and subject, 'records-history build (D111)', 'declared intervention too' and 'squash'. No merge is made and the bare remote branch still holds the intervention commit. With no extra commits listed, the message names the refused head.

criteria.criterion: README.md or CHANGELOG.md document the new land behavior and the D111 interim refusal, so a maintainer can find why land refused.
criteria.evidence: README adds a paragraph, 'Which commit land --pr judges', covering current-head judging and guarding, never replacing a newer head, and the D111 refusal with what it names. CHANGELOG's Fixed section records the change, cites PR #149 and squash 02837e0, and says the replace path is removed.

criteria.criterion: cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check are clean; cargo test passes for the changed crates (the pre-existing reading_inputs_digest failure is noted if it persists).
criteria.evidence: fmt printed nothing, clippy finished clean, and every test suite in athena-core and athena-cli reported 0 failed. The reading_inputs_digest failure did not appear. These results are about this snapshot.

findings.summary: The old replace helpers are left as dead code, and design docs still describe the replace path.
findings.evidence: Grep finds check_replace, ReplaceRequest and push_if_remote_at still defined with no caller in land. The design docs still describe the compare-and-swap replacement of the job's branch head.

findings.summary: An error while listing extra commits is swallowed, so the refusal can give a wrong reason.
findings.evidence: commits_after(...).unwrap_or_default(). If ensure_commit or git log fails, extras is empty and the message says the head is 'older than it or unrelated to it', which may be false. Land still refuses and merges nothing.

findings.summary: A remote head that is an older ancestor of the landing commit is now refused instead of updated, and the README's recovery advice is vague.
findings.evidence: The removed test a_rerun_replaces_a_bare_candidate_head... covered this flow. The request's 'anything other' wording allows refusing it. But the advice 'land the job's own commit, or wait for D111' doesn't say how to get the PR branch back to the landing commit.

findings.summary: Scope: one changed file is outside the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: It isn't in the expected deliverables but was a planned file. The change only adapts the test double to the changed Remote trait. Listed files land.rs, main.rs and landing_tests.rs did not change, and no criterion needed them.

findings.summary: The guard test can't show which value the merge guard came from.
findings.evidence: merge_heads == [cand1], and cand1 is also the stored head and the job's commit. Because land refuses any other head, they are always equal in practice.

summary: The candidate does what was asked, and I recommend accepting it. land --pr now reads the pull request's current head from the remote branch, stores it, and uses it as the merge guard; there is no longer any way to replace a remote head. When the head is anything other than the job's landing commit, land refuses. The refusal shows the head's check state, lists each extra commit by short id and subject (or names the head itself when there are none), and gives the D111 reason, which holds for declared interventions too. I ran the five new land_pr tests (including one end to end over real git with an intervention commit), the full athena-core and athena-cli test suites, fmt and clippy; all passed on this snapshot, and the reading_inputs_digest failure did not appear. Findings are minor only: the old replace helpers are left as dead code and design docs still describe them; an error while listing extra commits is swallowed, so the refusal can give a wrong reason; a remote head older than the landing commit is now refused, and the README's recovery advice for that case is vague; and external_calls.rs changed outside the deliverables list, only to adapt a test double to the changed trait.
